data.long_meaning: The name Digvijay is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘dig’ meaning direction or all and ‘vijay’ meaning victory. data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Digvijay total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Digvijay holds a significant place in Indian culture as it embodies the spirit of victory and resilience. In Hindu mythology, the God of Victory, Vinayaka or Ganesha, is invoked before beginning any new venture or endeavor to ensure success. The name Digvijay symbolizes that same spirit of triumph and contests that no matter what obstacles may come in the way, one can achieve victory with the right attitude and determination.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Digvijay holds even more significance. It represents the idea that true victory comes not from material success or wealth, but from a deep sense of inner peace and spiritual growth. Those named Digvijay are encouraged to live a virtuous and righteous life, to uphold the values of dharma and truth, and to strive towards spiritual enlightenment. In this way, the name Digvijay serves as a constant reminder to pursue the path of righteousness and to seek victory in the spiritual realm, rather than just the material one.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Digvijay: Victor of all battles, radiant with the triumph of dharma. Embodying the invincible spirit of righteousness that conquers all obstacles.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'दिग्विजय' (digvijaya), which is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and mythologies. It is often associated with the god Vishnu, who is known to have achieved victory in all directions.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Digvijay was a king of the Satavahana dynasty in the 2nd century AD. The name Digvijay carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ruled over a significant part of the Indian subcontinent

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Digvijay remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Digvijay in Kathmandu, Nepal attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Digvijay, which means "Victory through Dharma". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
